title: System Architecture
purpose: Show the deployed application layers and their connections.
note: The browser receives server-rendered Handlebars pages. React, Nginx and a cloud service are not part of this deployment.

title: Class Diagram
purpose: Describe the four database models and their actual relationships.
note: User to Request is an email-based application association, not a database foreign key. Appointment and Attachment are defined models with incomplete feature wiring.

title: Component Diagram
purpose: Show software modules and library dependencies.
note: Controllers contain both business logic and page rendering. This is one Express application rather than separate frontend and backend services.

title: Deployment Diagram
purpose: Map runtime artifacts to Docker containers, network and storage.
note: The app is bound to the host loopback address. MySQL has no published host port. Database storage survives container recreation.

title: Object Diagram
purpose: Illustrate one possible data snapshot with object instances.
note: All names, IDs and values on this page are fictional examples. A request owner is located by matching email; it has no userId column.

title: Package Diagram
purpose: Group repository modules into their existing folders.
note: Arrows indicate source dependencies. The config folder includes a mock collection interface; the active relational connection is models/db.js.

title: Composite Structure Diagram
purpose: Expand the internal parts of the Express application classifier.
note: Internal parts represent existing module responsibilities. The connection to MySQL is a required external interface, not an internal database copy.

title: Profile Diagram
purpose: Demonstrate optional UML vocabulary for the civil registry domain.
note: Proposed documentation profile only. SmartCivi does not implement or require a custom UML profile. Tagged values describe model elements, not runtime behavior.

title: Data Flow Diagram Context
purpose: Define the system boundary and external data exchanges.
note: Context-level DFD. Payment details stay inside SmartCivi in this prototype; no external payment gateway is connected.

title: Data Flow Diagram Level One
purpose: Trace account, request, review and payment data to persistent stores.
note: D1 and D2 are MySQL tables. Appointment and attachment stores are omitted here because these end-to-end flows are not fully connected in the controllers.

title: Use Case Diagram
purpose: Map external actors to the main system goals.
note: Core use cases reflect existing account and request controllers. Appointment scheduling, uploads and external payment processing remain supplementary design goals.

title: Activity Diagram
purpose: Follow the request submission workflow including validation and storage failures.
note: This activity describes POST /request and the subsequent confirmation page. It does not claim that administrator review occurs during submission.

title: Sequence Diagram
purpose: Show chronological request submission from browser to MySQL and the confirmation redirect.
note: Successful submission path. The browser subsequently follows the redirect with a separate GET, which reads the saved row and renders its confirmation page.

title: State Machine Diagram
purpose: Model the normal request status lifecycle and payment branches.
note: The lifecycle is descriptive. The current admin endpoint accepts arbitrary status strings and does not enforce every transition shown. Pending is the model default; submission writes lowercase pending.

title: Communication Diagram
purpose: Show the collaboration links for a valid request submission using numbered messages.
note: Message numbering expresses order. This is the same scenario as the sequence diagram, presented as a communication network.

title: Interaction Overview Diagram
purpose: Coordinate major interactions across the request and payment journey.
note: Each ref frame denotes a separate interaction, not an automatic background task. Rejection and administrator status changes are explicit decisions.

title: Timing Diagram
purpose: Compare session, request and record state at ordered events.
note: Logical event ordering only. No measured latency, deadline, real-time guarantee or external payment timing is implied. Session storage resets when the app process is recreated.

title: Requirement Diagram
purpose: Trace system requirements to the components that satisfy them.
note: SysML requirement diagrams are included because the assignment reference lists them. They are requirements traceability models rather than behavioral UML diagrams.
